steps.prompt: If you wrote an essay explaining how to look after a dog, what three parts would you explain? If you wrote a true story about a dog, what would the story be about underneath?

cards.title: Informative thesis: topic + parts
cards.body: An informative thesis doesn’t take a side. It names the topic and the parts you will explain: “Volcanoes form in three stages.” “Honeybees help farms by pollinating crops, making honey and supporting other wildlife.” Each part becomes a body paragraph.

cards.title: Narrative focus: what it meant
cards.body: A narrative essay’s focus tells the reader what the true story is really about: what it taught you, how it changed you. “The summer I broke my arm taught me to ask for help.” The story shows it; the focus names it.

cards.title: Same topic, three theses
cards.telling: Cities should build more parks because parks cool streets and bring neighbours together. (argumentative)
cards.showing: City parks help people in three ways: shade, exercise and community. (informative) · The day our street got a park, I met my best friend. It taught me that places shape people. (narrative)
cards.note: Argue: should + because. Explain: the parts. Tell: what it meant.

prompts: What is the difference between arguing and explaining?
Think of a true moment from your life. What did it teach you?
